commit.message:
docs(macos): neither model loads under Ollama, and why

Once a model fits the GPU whole this fork adds nothing to its speed -
the layer tuner is overridden, the budget planning is moot, and
metal-split-mmap.patch only applies to a CPU split - so Kolibri Q3_K_M
at 51 of 51 layers is plain llama.cpp with Metal.  Tried under Ollama
0.35.1 on the same Mac:

- Kolibri Q3_K_M: `ollama create` succeeds and validates nothing; the
  first request fails with "unknown model architecture: 'kolibri1'".
  Upstream llama.cpp has only an open feature request (#29922); the
  architecture exists in this fork's patch and nowhere else.
- Qwen Q2_0: `ollama create` fails before any architecture check, with
  "unsupported tensor blk.0.ffn_down_exps.weight size overflows" - its
  own GGUF parser.  Probably GGML_TYPE_Q2_0 = 42 (of 43) being newer
  than Ollama's vendored llama.cpp; the split layout may contribute and
  this was not isolated.  qwen4exp itself is upstream.

So the unlock for Kolibri is upstreaming kolibri1-llama.cpp.patch, which
would serve Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp at once.

Also recorded: `ollama rm` leaves the blob behind unreferenced, which
cost 35 GB until it was deleted by hand.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

bench(macos): Kolibri-1 at 3 bits, 32 -> 59 tok/s on a 48 GB Mac

Setup installs Kolibri-1 Q4_K_M, and its 44.2 GiB cannot go on a 48 GB
Mac's GPU at any Metal limit: it runs as a split, reads experts through
the page cache, and metal-split-mmap.patch copies the GPU's weights out
of the file instead of mapping it.  The official GGUF repo has nothing
between Q4_K_M and Q8_0, so both 3-bit files were quantized locally from
the official Q8_0 (83.1 GB).

  Q4_K_M  44.2 GiB   1 layer    ~32 tok/s   (the tuner's pick)
  Q3_K_M  34.9 GiB   51 layers   56.7-60.2  <- now the config
  Q3_K_S  31.5 GiB   51 layers   62.4-63.1

-c 65536, KV int8, through serve/server.py.  Q3_K_M was verified at the
stock 37.44 GiB working set, so it needs no sysctl and survives a
reboot; the footprint reads 0.9 GiB for a 35 GiB model and the SSD is
silent, which is the file being mapped rather than copied.

Kolibri-1 was always the faster model per token - at ONE GPU layer, with
the CPU doing nearly all of it, it already matched Qwen Q2_0 running
entirely on the GPU - and was only held back by not fitting.

Quality over six German tasks at temperature 0: Q3_K_M is not
distinguishable from Q4_K_M on the five that could be compared, Q3_K_S
is correct but consistently terser, which matches llama-quantize's own
+0.66 against +1.63 ppl.  Six prompts rule out obvious damage and no
more.

Notes for repeating it: llama-quantize is not in engine/ after a normal
setup (cmake --build build-llama --target llama-quantize), a split input
needs no merging because llama_model_loader finds the other shards from
split.count, and --allow-requantize is required since Q8_0 is already
quantized - this is requantization, not a clean basis.

setup.py is unchanged: offering this would mean shipping a quantization
step, and the numbers come from one Mac.  docs/MACOS.md points at it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

bench(macos): Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at 34 tok/s, by mapping the file

Qwen ran at 10.6 tok/s on a 48 GB M5 Pro: Q2_0 instead of IQ2_XS and
every layer on the GPU bring it to 34.0, measured through
serve/server.py.

  before   IQ2_XS   24 layers   ctx 131072   int8   10.6
  now      Q2_0     49 layers   ctx  65536   int8   34.0
  (with iogpu.wired_limit_mb=41984)  ctx 131072      33.8

Of that, the quantization is worth ~10% (11.8 at the same 24 layers) and
the layer count the rest.  Neither of the two obvious causes was it: the
Metal kernels do make Q2_0's dot product far cheaper than IQ2_XS's
codebook lookups, and the 26.8 GiB per_layer_token_embd table reads only
0.2-0.3 MB per token once the model is on the GPU.

What it is: the threshold where nearly every tensor in the file belongs
to the GPU's buffer and llama.cpp maps the file into it instead of
copying the GPU's weights out (metal-split-mmap.patch does the copying
below it).  Q2_0, -c 32768: 44 layers 23.8 tok/s, 32.2 GiB footprint,
31.7 s to load; 47 layers 29.2 tok/s, 0.9 GiB, 11.8 s; 49 layers 33.4.
Q2_0 is needed to reach that threshold at all - 35.0 GiB against
IQ2_XS's 36.5, under a 37.44 GiB working set.

So a model that nearly fits a Mac wants every layer on the GPU and a
context that fits, not the layer tuner's split - the opposite of the
right answer for Kolibri-1, which does not fit at all.

Context is a memory question only: 65536 and 131072 run at the same
speed, and 131072 needs the raised iogpu.wired_limit_mb, which a reboot
undoes - so the config keeps 65536.  KV quantization is not a lever
(q4 and int8 measure the same; int8 for the quality).  Quality checked
at five tasks, temperature 0, both quantizations: no difference.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

bench(macos): a GPU layer count has to be measured in the server

Measuring llama-server on its own says Kolibri-1 Q4_K_M wants 30 GPU
layers on a 48 GB M5 Pro and runs at 43-48 tok/s.  Measured through
serve/server.py, the same prompts and the same count give 16-22, and
the best count is the 1-5 the standalone tool rates slowest:

  GPU layers   llama-server alone   in the server
           1                 32.0   32.2
           5          not measured  32.4
           9           28.3, 26.1   26.5 - 28.3
          30           43.7 - 47.9  15.7 - 22.5, alternating

The two agree at low counts and part by a factor of two at high ones.
A GPU layer costs the page cache the CPU-side experts are read through:
30 layers wire 28.7 GiB, which with the ~15.5 GiB read through the cache
is 44.2 of 48 GiB - enough with nothing else resident, not enough with
the server and the runner beside it.  Wired GPU memory cannot be paged
out, so everything else gives way and the replies alternate between
~16 and ~22 tok/s as paging comes and goes.  The standalone figures are
reproducible (9 layers first and last in one run: 28.3 and 26.1), so
this is a benchmark leaving out part of the system it predicts, not
drift.

So the runner's tuner was right to keep 1 layer here, and its rule - a
busy SSD at the start count means walk towards fewer layers - reads this
Mac correctly.  LayerTuner is unchanged: a change to make it always
probe upwards first was written against the standalone curve's peak at
30 layers, which the server never sees, and reverted.

mac_split_bench.py says all this in its docstring now, and two real bugs
in it are fixed: it printed a "runner's count" computed differently from
the runner (26 against the runner's 10 for Qwen, ignoring the
START_GPU_SHARE path a model read from the SSD takes), and it left
--threads to llama.cpp instead of passing the runner's count, which on
an M5 Pro is worth about as much as the layer split.

Also measured: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ2_XS is not held back by the
28.8 GB per-layer embedding table the old handover suspected.  At 1 GPU
layer, where both methods agree, it reads 5.6 MB per token and writes
6.5 tok/s while Kolibri-1 reads a comparable 3.2 MB and writes 32.0 -
five times as fast with more active parameters per token (3.46B against
~2.4B).  What is left between them is the quantization: Q4_K_M scales
blocks, IQ2_XS looks codebook entries up.  A k-quant of the same model
(Q2_0) side by side would settle it and was not measured.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(native): Kolibri-1's real hidden size and expert FFN

check_architecture refused the real Kolibri-1 GGUF with
"kolibri1.embedding_length = 2560, expected 6144", so the native engine
would not have run the model at all.  The file's own metadata says
embedding_length 2560 and expert_feed_forward_length 512; the 6144 was
n_head * head_dim, the width attn_q projects TO, mistaken for n_embd
(attn_q.weight is [2560, 6144]).

check_one (src/core/layout.cpp) already writes its shape checks
symbolically, and with 2560 / 512 all ten of them match the real
tensors exactly - ffn_gate_exps [2560, 512, 384], attn_k [2560, 512],
ffn_down_shexp [512, 2560], attn_output [6144, 2560].  With the old
values every one failed.

Checked on a 48 GB M5 Pro against Kolibri-1 Q4_K_M: compiling
check_architecture against the file prints the refusal above with 6144
and accepts with 2560; src/core/layout.cpp compiles clean.  The kernels
themselves are untried - strata_core, which builds layout.cpp, is only
built with CUDA or HIP, so this needs a PC to run end to end.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(macos): count only what has to be in memory

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's per-layer embedding table stays in the GGUF and
llama.cpp reads its rows while it answers (TENSOR_READ_LAZY, tensors
over 4 GiB).  The runner counted it as model memory: the Coder IQ1_M
(58.4 GB in the files: a 28.8 GB table, 25.1 GB of experts, 4.5 GB of
the rest) looked too large for a 48 GB Mac and ran the SSD tuning with
13 of 49 layers on the GPU.  It now subtracts that table (tensor_sizes,
lazy_bytes): 29.6 GB to hold, fully on the GPU on 48 GB and 64 GB Macs;
32-36 GB Macs are unchanged.  The memory line shows both parts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(setup): Kolibri-1 and macOS after the 0.1.39 merge

- Step 7 stopped on a model without an n-gram table (Kolibri-1): 0.1.39's
  rotational-disk check (#605) stat()ed its PLE file, which is None
  there.  It is skipped for such a model.
- get_llama_cpp used main()'s local is_mac: a NameError on every setup
  run with third_party/llama.cpp already there.  A module-level MAC.
- macOS never uses the low-RAM mode: the Metal runner reads the GGUF and
  sizes the GPU's share itself; the mode's experts.bin (45.7 GB for
  Kolibri-1 Q4_K_M) was never read.  The pack is ~100 MB now.

Checked on a 32 GB M1 Max: ./setup.sh --yes --family kolibri --model
Q4_K_M --gguf-dir ... --no-start runs through; the server then answers
a chat completion and a Responses API request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge upstream Strata v0.1.39 (Niko1221/Strata) into the macOS port

Upstream 0.1.39: faster decode and long prompts, parallel requests,
older and other hardware as experimental opt-ins, the OpenAI Responses
API, Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, a Settings view, and fixes.

macOS adaptations in the merge:
- CMake: kq_avx1.cpp's AVX flags only on x86; kq_avx1.cpp compiles to a
  stub on arm64 (only called behind cpu_avx1_ok, false there).
- expert_layout.cpp: cpu_isa_cap for every platform; cpu_avx1_ok and
  cpu_sse42_ok (new) inside the x86 block, stubs on arm64.
- expert_source.cpp: the Mach host statistics fill 0.1.39's HostMemory.
- pool.cpp: the Mach affinity tags beside the new Windows CPU Sets and
  Linux affinity code, with 0.1.39's ThreadAffinity signatures.
- server.py: the model switch beside the Settings view (/config) and
  the control-body check; the switch's fallback around the engine start
  with effort_end_args.
- setup.py / strata_mcp.py: Kolibri-1 after Unsloth (upstream's menu
  numbers), no older-CPU build or CUDA libraries on a Mac; Kolibri-1 is
  a 47.5 GB download (it said 44.5).
- strata_runner.py: an unknown engine command (VRAM, #533) is answered
  with ERR instead of being dropped.
- Docs: upstream's text with the macOS parts kept; the claim that
  Kolibri-1 fits a 48 GB Mac completely is corrected.

Built on macOS (arm64): strata-gguf, strata-plan, strata-dequant,
strata_kernels_cpu; direct_file_async_test, platform_memory_test,
expert_multi_test, pool_stress pass.  All tools/test_setup_*.py, the
runner and MCP tests pass; serve/ tests pass except the AMD telemetry
pair and test_responses' json_schema case, which fail the same way on
plain v0.1.39 on this Mac.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(macos): threads from the fastest core level only

Counting every performance level macOS does not call "Efficiency" gave
15 threads on an M5 Pro (5 + 10 cores), and Kolibri-1 wrote ~15 tok/s
(9 GPU layers) where it had written ~24-35 with 5 threads (other GPU
splits).  Every step waits for its slowest thread, so the runner uses
the cores of hw.perflevel0 again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(macos): tune the GPU layer count from the replies

A model larger than the memory reads the experts it does not hold
through the page cache from the SSD, and every GPU layer holds all its
experts and takes that memory from the page cache.  Kolibri-1 Q4_K_M on
a 32 GB M1 Max: 0 / 6 / 12 GPU layers gave 25.7 / 26.1 / 8.2 tok/s with
0.5 / 9.3 / 81.9 MB per token read from the SSD.

The runner now starts with 20% of the memory left after the reserve for
GPU layers and tunes the count (LayerTuner): each count is measured over
256 output tokens (tok/s and the llama-server process's pageins), then,
20 s after the last reply, llama-server restarts one step towards more
GPU layers when the SSD is quiet, else fewer, while that is faster; it
keeps the fastest (fewest layers within 3%) in engine/metal-tune.json
per model and memory size.  On the M1 Max: 5 -> 9 -> 1, kept 1 GPU
layer at 31.7 tok/s, 0.4 MB per token from the SSD.

Threads: the cores of every performance level macOS does not call
"Efficiency".  An madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) prefetch of the CPU experts was
measured slower (6.86 vs 7.95 tok/s) and is not included.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
